edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a harmful direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: workers or residents exposed to trichloroethylene
edges.mechanism: Kidney metabolism of trichloroethylene generates reactive intermediates capable of tubular DNA injury, matching the observed concern about renal cell carcinoma.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2012 Karami meta analysis in Occup Environ Med already points to trichloroethylene exposure tracks with higher risk or worse outcomes, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Residual confounding and reverse causation remain possible in some observational studies, so the main readout is direction and plausibility rather than one exact risk number.
